title: Role-aware Audit Envelope Exporter Spec
content:
Purpose:
This is a working spec for a lightweight, role-aware audit envelope exporter (RAAE). The exporter's job is to: capture and normalize audit events emitted across services, enrich them with RBAC v2 context, pack them into compact signed envelopes to preserve integrity, and stream/batch export to downstream SIEMs and long-term evidence stores.

Goals:
- Preserve RBAC context and actionable claims in every exported record so downstream security teams can apply least-privilege analytics.
- Provide a compact envelope format that supports streaming with small overhead and deterministic ordering per resource.
- Enable multi-destination routing (SIEM, archival S3, internal forensic queue) with per-destination policies and backpressure handling.
- Be minimally invasive: library + sidecar pattern for services and a standalone daemon for infra components.

Non-goals:
- Full proof-chain cryptographic ledger (we may add later). No blockchain-style consensus in v1.
- Replacing existing heavy-weight evidence pipelines—this is a lightweight real-time complement.

High-level design:
1) Emitters (services, infra components) produce normalized audit events to a local sidecar or in-process library. Events MUST include the minimal canonical audit fields (see schema below).
2) Sidecar/enrichment layer attaches RBAC v2 claims: role_id, role_revision, scope, request_policy (if available). It also maps SCIM/principal IDs to human names via a bounded cache.
3) Enveloper (central aggregator or per-cluster daemon) sequences events into ordered envelopes. Each envelope includes a header, a compact merkle-lite hash chain for quick integrity checks, and an optional signed trailer for verification.
4) Exporter sinks route envelopes to configured destinations. Streaming exporters use HTTP/2+ gRPC with flow control; batch exporters flush to S3 or archival queues.

Schema (canonical minimal event):
- event_id: string (UUIDv4)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- service: string (logical service name)
- resource: string (resource id / path)
- action: string (create/update/delete/authn/authz/role-assignment/… )
- principal_id: string (SCIM id / internal id)
- principal_type: string (user | service | key)
- rbac_context: string (JSON-stringified RBAC v2 claim set OR reference token)
- outcome: string (success | failure | conditional)
- meta: string (optional short freeform, base64 if binary)
- seq: string (per-resource monotonic counter, optional)
- collector_origin: string (hostname/container/task-id)

Envelope format (compact JSON + binary-friendly attachments):
- envelope_id: UUID
- created_at: ISO8601
- source_cluster: string
- sequence_range: "seq_start-seq_end" (per-resource when present)
- header_claims: array[string] (important claims for routing like tenant_id, role_revision)
- events: array[event objects as above] (size limited, see batching)
- hash_chain_tip: base64 (sha256 over previous tip + this envelope bytes)
- signature: optional base64 (ed25519)

Design notes on RBAC integration:
- rbac_context should be a compact projection of RBAC v2 for the event: {roles: [role_ids], permissions_snapshot: [perm_hashes], evaluation_time: ISO8601}. Storing a full role graph inline is discouraged.
- When available, include role_revision so downstream audits can resolve the exact policy used. The exporter will retain a minimal policy snapshot cache for lookups during forensic queries.
- For high-cardinality events (API keys, service accounts) we keep principal_id stable and add principal_fingerprint to help de-duplicate.

Routing & destination policies:
- Destinations are defined in config with priority and filters. Example: send all admin-role-change events to SIEM-primary + archival, low-sensitivity telemetry to analytics only.
- Per-tenant routing: tenant_id should be in header_claims; exporter must respect data residency flags and choose region-appropriate sinks.
- Fallbacks: if primary SIEM endpoint fails, fall back to secondary buffer (durable local queue) and notify SRE. Do not silently drop admin/forensic events.

Streaming semantics & backpressure:
- Use gRPC streaming with explicit ack windows. Each envelope has a window token. Receiver acks up to X envelopes; exporter stops sending when unacked size exceeds limit.
- If downstream is slow, the exporter switches to disk-backed batching and continues to accept events up to a configured disk quota.
- Operators can configure eviction: for non-critical telemetry, keep FIFO; for critical audit (role changes, auth failures), use guaranteed persist-first semantics.

Retention controls and privacy:
- Envelopes destined for SIEM may be redacted based on data-class tags (PII, secrets). Redaction rules are config-driven with allowlists for forensic roles.
- Retention metadata is attached as envelope header: {retention_class: short, expires_at: ISO8601}. Exporter enforces local purge and signals archival store TTL.

Security: signing & integrity
- Envelopes contain a hash_chain_tip computed as sha256(prev_tip || envelope_bytes); this gives quick tamper-evidence without full merkle proofs.
- Signing is optional for v1, recommended for enterprise tenants. Use ed25519 keys stored in KMS/HSM. Signatures attach to the trailer as base64.
- Key rotation: exporter keeps recent public keys in the header_claims with key_id so verifiers can pick correct key.

Operational concerns & monitoring:
- Metrics to emit: envelopes_produced, envelopes_exported_{dest}, exporter_queue_depth, disk_backlog_bytes, export_retries, signature_errors, redact_hits.
- Traces: sample full-envelop trace for slow exports (>=500ms) and every sign/verify failure.
- Alerting rules: exporter_queue_depth > 1000 for 5m, export_retries > 50/min, signature_failure_rate > 0.1%

Migration plan from existing pipelines:
- Phase 0 (pilot): Run RAAE side-by-side with current collector for a small subset of services (auth, iam, console). Verify parity for key event types.
- Phase 1 (selected rollout): Enable streaming to SIEM-secondary and archival for security team review.
- Phase 2 (cutover): Switch primary SIEM flow, keep legacy pipeline in read-only/backfill mode for 30d.

Developer-facing APIs / CLI examples:
- Local sidecar: POST /v1/audit -> returns 202 + seq token
- Enveloper admin: GET /v1/status -> {queue_depth, last_exported_seq}
- CLI: raaectl tail --service auth --follow
- Simple export config snippet (YAML):
  destinations:
    - name: siem-primary
      type: gRPC
      url: siem-primary.internal:443
      priority: 1
      filters: ["rbac.role:admin", "action:role-assignment"]

Testing & validation:
- Unit: schema conformance, RBAC projection tests, hash_chain deterministic tests.
- Integration: end-to-end small cluster, simulate SIEM failures and verify disk queueing & replay.
- Privacy: redaction rules verified against representative PII payloads.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a compact binary envelope (CBOR) in v1 for bandwidth-sensitive tenants? Pros: smaller. Cons: harder to audit in text.
- Exact limits for envelope size and per-resource sequencing when resources cross services.
- How to expose envelope-level proofs to customers (SaaS tenants) without leaking internal mapping?

References & links:
- JIRA: JIRA-SEC-889 (exporter prototype)
- Confluence: CON-4321 "Audit export patterns"
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-exporter/pull/14

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: we favor incremental deployability and operator safety. Expect heuristics to change after pilot.
- Comments inline are fine; tag JIRA-SEC-889 when you want a follow-up.
